subject: Government
title: Power, Authority, Legitimacy, and Sovereignty
outline: Meaning and sources of political power
Weber's three types of legitimate authority
Types of sovereignty: legal, political, internal, external, popular
Relationship between power, authority and legitimacy

modules.title: Power and Its Sources
modules.html:
Power is the ability to influence or control the behaviour of others, with or without their consent. It is the raw capacity to make people do what they would not otherwise do. Power may rest on persuasion, on reward, or ultimately on coercion.

Sources of political power include:

  • The constitution and law — offices created by law carry defined powers.
  • Coercion / control of the instruments of violence — army, police.
  • Wealth and control of economic resources.
  • Knowledge, expertise and information — the bureaucrat's file, the professional's advice.
  • Charisma and personality — the magnetic leader.
  • Numbers — the votes of a large following; the strength of a trade union.
  • Tradition, religion and custom.

Characteristics of power: it is relational (always over someone), dynamic (it shifts), it may be legitimate or illegitimate, and it is exercised in every human organisation, not only in government.

examples.q: A wealthy businessman funds a party and influences a minister's decision. Which source of power is at work?
examples.a: Economic power – control of wealth used to influence political decision-making.

modules.title: Authority and Legitimacy
modules.html:
Authority is rightful power — power that is recognised as lawful by those over whom it is exercised. Power without authority is naked force; authority is power clothed in right.

Max Weber identified three pure types of legitimate authority:

TypeBasis of obedienceExample
TraditionalLong-established custom and inherited status.The Sultan of Sokoto; the Ooni of Ife.
CharismaticExceptional personal qualities of the leader.Nnamdi Azikiwe; Mahatma Gandhi.
Legal-rationalImpersonal rules and formal office.The President under the 1999 Constitution; a permanent secretary.

Other classifications include coercive authority (based on fear), delegated authority (transferred from a superior) and political, administrative and judicial authority depending on the office held.

Legitimacy is the popular belief that a government has the right to rule and ought to be obeyed. It is acquired through free and fair elections, constitutional procedure, effective performance, tradition and popular acceptance. A regime may hold power (a coup-installed junta) yet lack legitimacy; and a legitimate government that loses its coercive capacity may lose power. Governments seek legitimacy because it makes obedience voluntary and cheap.

examples.q: A military government organises a referendum which it wins overwhelmingly. What is it seeking?
examples.a: Legitimacy – popular endorsement that converts its de facto power into rightful authority.

modules.title: Sovereignty and Its Types
modules.html:
Sovereignty is the supreme, ultimate and unlimited legal power of the state to make and enforce laws within its territory, and its independence from external control. Jean Bodin (1576) first developed the concept systematically.

Characteristics: absoluteness, permanence, universality (it binds everyone in the territory), indivisibility, inalienability, and exclusiveness.

TypeMeaning
Internal sovereigntySupremacy over all persons and associations within the territory.
External sovereigntyFreedom from control by any other state; the basis of independence.
Legal sovereigntyResides in the body legally competent to make law – in Nigeria, the National Assembly acting under the constitution.
Political sovereigntyResides in the electorate, whose votes ultimately determine who makes the law.
Popular sovereigntyThe doctrine that ultimate power belongs to the people as a whole.
De jure sovereigntySovereignty recognised by law.
De facto sovereigntySovereignty actually exercised, e.g. by a successful coup leader before recognition.

examples.q: Which type of sovereignty does the Nigerian electorate exercise?
examples.a: Political (and popular) sovereignty – legal sovereignty belongs to the National Assembly, but its members hold office only by the votes of the electorate.

modules.title: Limitations on Sovereignty
modules.html:
Although sovereignty is theoretically absolute, in practice it is limited by:

  • The constitution — entrenched provisions and fundamental rights restrain the legislature.
  • International law and treaties — membership of the UN, AU and ECOWAS imposes obligations.
  • Public opinion and the electorate — no government can persistently defy the governed.
  • Federalism — powers are shared between the centre and the states.
  • Economic dependence — loan conditions from the IMF or World Bank restrict policy choice.
  • Custom, religion and morality.
  • Military and technological weakness relative to great powers.

Relationship summary: power is the capacity to compel; authority is power recognised as rightful; legitimacy is the belief that sustains authority; and sovereignty is the supreme form of authority claimed by the state. Legitimate authority backed by sovereignty produces stable government.

examples.q: How does ECOWAS membership limit Nigeria's sovereignty?
examples.a: Nigeria accepts protocols on free movement, trade and, at times, collective security decisions, so it cannot legislate freely on those matters without breaching treaty obligations.

modules.title: Types and characteristics of authority
modules.html:
Types and characteristics of authority is a key part of Power, Authority, Legitimacy, and Sovereignty (SSS 1, Government). Master the meaning, the main points and how it is tested in JAMB and WAEC questions on this topic.

Key points

  • Characteristics of power: it is relational (always over someone), dynamic (it shifts), it may be legitimate or illegitimate, and it is exercised in every human organisation, not only in government.
  • Authority is rightful power — power that is recognised as lawful by those over whom it is exercised.
  • Power without authority is naked force; authority is power clothed in right.
  • Max Weber identified three pure types of legitimate authority: Type Basis of obedience Example Traditional Long-established custom and inherited status.
  • Other classifications include coercive authority (based on fear), delegated authority (transferred from a superior) and political, administrative and judicial authority depending on the office held.

Worked example

Q: Power that is accepted as rightful is called
A: Authority — Authority is legitimate or rightful power.

Q: Max Weber's three types of authority are
A: Traditional, charismatic, legal-rational — Weber's classic triad.

examples.q: Power that is accepted as rightful is called
examples.a: Authority — Authority is legitimate or rightful power.

examples.q: Max Weber's three types of authority are
examples.a: Traditional, charismatic, legal-rational — Weber's classic triad.

modules.html:

  • A regime may hold power (a coup-installed junta) yet lack legitimacy; and a legitimate government that loses its coercive capacity may lose power.
  • Governments seek legitimacy because it makes obedience voluntary and cheap.
  • Type Meaning Internal sovereignty Supremacy over all persons and associations within the territory.

quiz.q: Power that is accepted as rightful is called
quiz.solution: Authority is legitimate or rightful power.

quiz.q: Max Weber's three types of authority are
quiz.solution: Weber's classic triad.

quiz.q: The authority of an Emir rests mainly on
quiz.solution: Inherited custom is the basis of traditional authority.

quiz.q: Sovereignty was first systematically developed by
quiz.solution: Bodin, in Six Books of the Commonwealth (1576).

quiz.q: Legal sovereignty in Nigeria resides in the
options: National Assembly acting under the constitution
quiz.solution: The legislature is the legally competent law-making body.

quiz.q: Political sovereignty resides in the
quiz.solution: The voters ultimately determine who makes law.

quiz.q: Freedom of a state from external control is
quiz.solution: External sovereignty is independence.

quiz.q: A coup leader exercising control before recognition holds
quiz.solution: De facto means 'in fact' though not yet in law.

quiz.q: Which is NOT a characteristic of sovereignty?
quiz.solution: Sovereignty is indivisible.

quiz.q: Legitimacy is best acquired through
quiz.solution: Popular consent expressed in credible elections.

quiz.q: Charismatic authority depends on
quiz.solution: Exceptional personal appeal is its basis.

quiz.q: Which of the following limits sovereignty in practice?
quiz.solution: All three constrain the exercise of sovereign power.

quiz.q: Power based on the control of the army is
quiz.solution: Control of instruments of violence gives coercive power.

quiz.q: Popular sovereignty means that ultimate power belongs to
quiz.solution: The doctrine locates supreme power in the people.

quiz.q: A permanent secretary's authority is
quiz.solution: It derives from formal office and impersonal rules.

quiz.q: The chief difference between power and authority is that authority
quiz.solution: Authority is power recognised as rightful.

quiz.q: Power sovereignty belongs to the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: People.

quiz.q: The supreme power of a state to make and enforce laws within its territory without external interference is known as _____.
quiz.solution: Sovereignty is the ultimate, absolute power of a state to govern itself and its people without being subject to any other authority.

quiz.q: Which organ of the United Nations has the power to veto decisions?
quiz.solution: The five permanent members of the UN Security Council (USA, UK, France, Russia, and China) possess veto power over substantive resolutions.

quiz.q: The power of a court to declare a law unconstitutional is known as _____.
quiz.solution: Judicial Review is the power of the judiciary to examine the actions of the legislative and executive branches and determine their constitutionality.

quiz.q: Sovereignty belongs to the _____.
quiz.solution: Sovereignty is the supreme and absolute power of a state to make and enforce laws within its territory without external interference.

quiz.q: The 'Power of the Purse' is exercised by the _____.
quiz.solution: The legislature has the constitutional power to approve the budget (income and expenditure) of the state.

quiz.q: The pre-colonial Oyo Empire utilized a system of _____ to limit the power of the Alaafin.
quiz.solution: The Oyo Mesi (Kingmakers) and the Ogboni cult acted as institutional checks on the power of the Alaafin.

quiz.q: The 'Power of the Purse' belongs to the _____.
quiz.solution: The legislature has the power of the purse, meaning it controls government spending and must approve the national budget.

quiz.q: The power of the courts to declare an act of the legislature unconstitutional is called _____.
quiz.solution: Judicial review allows the judiciary to examine the constitutionality of the actions of the other branches of government.

quiz.q: The symbol of authority in the legislature is:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2021). Correct answer: Mace.

quiz.q: Power is defined as:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: The ability to compel obedience.

quiz.q: Authority refers to:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Legitimate power.

quiz.q: The Mace is a symbol of authority in the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2022). Correct answer: Legislature.

quiz.q: The mace symbolizes authority in the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2023). Correct answer: Legislature.

quiz.q: The concept of 'Sovereignty' was first popularized by...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Jean Bodin.

quiz.q: The permanent members of the UN Security Council have the power of...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: The Veto.

quiz.q: A system where power is shared between the center and the component units is...
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2024). Correct answer: Federal.

quiz.q: Sovereignty resides with the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: People.

quiz.q: The mace is the symbol of authority in the:
quiz.solution: Past question (JAMB 2025). Correct answer: Legislature.

quiz.q: Federalism is a system where power is:
quiz.solution: Past question (NECO 2025). Correct answer: Shared between Center and Units.

quiz.q: A system where power is concentrated at the center is:
quiz.solution: Past question (WAEC 2025). Correct answer: Unitary.

quiz.q: Which colonial power practiced the policy of Assimilation?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: France.

quiz.q: Sovereignty means?
options: Supreme legal authority of a state
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Supreme legal authority of a state.

quiz.q: Who has the power to appoint the Chairman of INEC?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: The President (subject to Senate confirmation).

quiz.q: What is ‘Veto Power’ in the context of the UN Security Council?
options: Power of a permanent member to block a resolution
Power to elect the Secretary-General alone
Power to declare war without a vote
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Power of a permanent member to block a resolution.

quiz.q: The power of the people to remove an elected official before their term ends is?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Recall.

quiz.q: What is the legal voting age in Nigeria?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 18.

quiz.q: Which regions first attained internal self-governance in 1957?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: West and East.

quiz.q: The legal instrument that brought the 1999 Constitution into force was?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: Decree 24 of 1999.

quiz.q: The ‘Two-Thirds of 19 states’ legal controversy occurred during the election of?
quiz.solution: Past-question bank (legacy TXT). Correct answer: 1979.

quiz.q: The process of depriving a person of his citizenship is known as _____.
quiz.solution: Denaturalization is the official act of depriving a person of citizenship, especially one acquired through naturalization, often due to criminal activity or fraud.

quiz.q: The primary function of the legislature is to _____.
quiz.solution: The legislature is the organ of government constitutionally empowered to debate, amend, and pass laws for the peace and good governance of the state.

quiz.q: The concept of 'Rule of Law' was popularized by _____.
quiz.solution: A.V. Dicey, in his book 'Introduction to the Study of the Law of the Constitution', outlined the three pillars of the rule of law: supremacy of the law, equality before the law, and protection of individual rights.

quiz.q: Which of the following is a permanent feature of the Civil Service?
quiz.solution: Anonymity means civil servants are neither praised nor blamed publicly for government policies; they work behind the scenes and remain invisible to the public.
